summary: Quote and LTP on the NIFTY index: the index channel gives the value, high, low and previous close, the day bucket the open; a Depth subscribe on the index is accepted on the desktop and refused on the web.

deviations.reason: Nubra's messages carry no trade time; the desktop sends its receipt time as ltt (NubraFeed leaves last_trade_time_ms 0, feed::bridge::ltt falls back to the tick's timestamp), the web sends no ltt. A receipt time must not pass as a trade time (audit P-08).
The web stamps Nubra frames with the message's own timestamp (obj.timestamp, receipt time only when it is 0); the desktop stamps its receipt time (audit P-08, still open).

The desktop's index frames add price_change and price_change_percent; the web's Nubra adapter sends no change for an index. Lead ruling 2026-11-09: not docs keys, the desktop follows the adapter (lane wire dialect, phase B).

The desktop's index frames add price_change and price_change_percent; the web's Nubra adapter sends no change for an index. Lead ruling 2026-11-09: not docs keys, the desktop follows the adapter (lane wire dialect, phase B).
Before the day bucket the web sends open 0 (ohlcv.get('open', 0)); a field the stream has not sent is left out (web openalgo#2376), as the desktop does.

Once the day bucket came the web sends the bucket's close (today's price) as close, ahead of prev_close (ohlcv.get('close', prev_close)); close is the previous day's close, which the desktop keeps sending (the audit's 'Nubra bucket close' note).
The web also sends the previous close as prev_close; the desktop sends it as close only. An alias for lane wire.
